TC-HIS-04.reason: Source adapter covers all expected items using read-only history API requests; E3 requires real history older than 25 hours and remains unprovable when no qualifying event exists. Reviewed cards, current baseline and explicit start are still required.

E1.method: GET a complete valid date range and assert HTTP 200, success=true and a list response (which may be empty).

E2.method: GET missing, reversed and malformed bounds and assert each returns HTTP 400, success=false and no data key.

E3.method: Find a real event older than 25 hours within 30-day history; assert the no-date/no-preset response excludes it and returns no event older than the 24-hour range with clock tolerance.

prerequisites: An initialized Super Admin account is available privately with system.history.
Existing alert history has at least one real event older than 25 hours but within the rolling 30-day range; no history is seeded or edited.
The API is served from the reviewed target and the device/server clocks differ by no more than the stated 5-minute tolerance.
recovery: Read-only GET requests only. No history, acknowledgement, or alert data is changed. POST logout, verify GET /api/user/me returns 401, dispose the browser context, and preserve expected login/logout audit entries.
TC-HIS-04.reviewed_by: Codex source review; not runtime acceptance
TC-HIS-04.procedure_review: Reviewed the complete TC-HIS-04 case and Alerts/Notifications History §3.3, plus Backend_Modules_and_Routes history contracts. The adapter checks a valid complete day range, missing/reversed/malformed bounds, then compares a known real event older than 25 hours with the no-date/no-preset API response. If the fixture event is absent, E3 is not inferred from an empty response and the attempt remains incomplete.
